A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same Ano-NAViLa work, with matching text, equations, tables, and figures. Neither contains appendices or the separately referenced supplementary material; the comparison covers all content in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original GastricLN and Camelyon16 experiments, including performance comparisons, computational measurements, ablations, and qualitative results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–4, including dataset evaluations, computational measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same term pools, frozen CONCH backbone, trainable MLP, text-augmented embeddings, contrastive objective, and anomaly scoring procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same GastricLN and Camelyon16 data, including the Camelyon16 macro-metastasis subset, for patch-level and whole-slide anomaly detection and localization.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GANomaly, STFPM, FastFlow, CFA, AnoDDPM, EfficientAD, and AnomalyCLIP. The scoring alternatives in Table 3 and the description of the zero-shot CONCH comparison also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical dataset splits, patch sizes, training settings, AUROC/AUPR metrics, heatmap preprocessing, and whole-slide score aggregation. Computational benchmarking still uses a batch size of 28.

E4.justification: The embedding-composition and anomaly-scoring ablations, localization examples, and image-text case studies are unchanged. Descriptions of erosion robustness and supplementary similarity analyses also match; the referenced supplementary displays are absent from both supplied files.

E5.justification: Both specify 95% confidence intervals using 2000-fold bootstrapping with replacement and present the same interval reporting. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-testing information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and qualitative figure content match. For example, Table 1 reports the same Ano-NAViLa GastricLN patch AUROC of 0.9681 and Camelyon16 maximum-score whole-slide AUROC of 0.8594.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–8 remain unchanged, including embedding weighting, the contrastive loss, and deviation scores. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness, and interpretability through normal and abnormal pathology knowledge.

C2.justification: Interpretations of embedding complementarity, generalization, localization, and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the same future directions concerning automated term pools, broader external validation, and VLM efficiency.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same text prompt, MLP architecture, Adam learning rate, batch size, gradient accumulation, single-epoch training, and GPU hardware. No implementation or code/data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to TQx and pathology VLMs, and all 51 numbered reference entries remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 21 August 2025 to v2 dated 28 October 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. The page layout is unchanged apart from negligible rendering differences.

improvement.justification: The supplied PDFs contain unchanged methods, experimental evidence, explanations, and conclusions. The version/date stamp update produces no meaningful difference in scientific quality, clarity, or reproducibility.
